figures.caption: Fig. 1: Sample classification results under grouped subject splitting. ROC-AUC is shown on the y-axis. The Friedman test found no significant differences between models (p = 0.093), although CytoBERT achieved the best average rank.
Table 2: Mean ROC-AUC of different models across downstream datasets.

Fig. 3: Critical difference diagrams comparing average model ranks across CyTOF datasets under ungrouped splitting (top) and grouped subject splitting (bottom). Lower rank indicates better average performance.

Fig. 2: Sample-level classification performance across CyTOF datasets under ungrouped splitting (top) and grouped subject splitting (bottom). The y-axis reports ROC-AUC. Grouped subject splitting ensures that samples from the same subject do not appear in both training and test folds.

Fig. 4: Overview of the CytoBERT pipeline, consisting of dataset curation and preprocessing, self-supervised masked expression-bin pretraining, and supervised fine-tuning for sample-level classification.
Table 1: Downstream CyTOF datasets. “Subjects” and “Samples” denote unique patients and sample files.
